questions.question:
“His face __________ with joy when the solution of the puzzle was __________ to him.”
The words that best fill the blanks in the above sentence are
questions.explanation:
Verbal Aptitude → Vocabulary

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given: A sentence with two blanks: "His face ____ with joy when the solution of the puzzle was ____ to him."
  • Find: The correct pair of words to fill the blanks.
  • Concepts used: English grammar, specifically past tense and past participle forms of verbs.

Solution

  • The first blank requires a verb indicating an action completed in the past that describes a face expressing joy. The base verb is "shine". The simple past tense of "shine" (in the context of glowing with emotion) is "shone".
  • The second blank follows "was", indicating passive voice, which requires the past participle form of the verb "show". The past participle of "show" is "shown".
  • Therefore, the correct pair is "shone" and "shown".

Final Answer

Answer: shone, shown
Correct option: (A)

The graph of a function f(x) is shown in the figure.



For f(x) to be a valid probability density function, the value of h is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: A PDF \(f(x)\) consisting of three disjoint right-angled triangles on the x-axis:
    • Triangle 1: base from \(x=0\) to \(1\), height \(= h\)
    • Triangle 2: base from \(x=1\) to \(2\), height \(= 2h\)
    • Triangle 3: base from \(x=2\) to \(3\), height \(= 3h\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(h\) such that \(f(x)\) is a valid PDF.

3. Core Concepts:

PDF Property: Total area under the PDF must equal 1.\[\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1\]

Area of a Triangle: \(A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(A_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times h = 0.5h\)
  2. \(A_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 2h = 1.0h\)
  3. \(A_3 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 3h = 1.5h\)
  4. Apply PDF property:\[0.5h + 1.0h + 1.5h = 1 \implies 3.0h = 1 \implies h = \dfrac{1}{3}\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(h = 1/3\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics — Skewness

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A graphical plot of a probability distribution \(f(x)\) vs \(x\) with a long tail extending to the right (Right Skew).
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode.

3. Core Concepts:

Right-Skewed (Positively Skewed) Distribution: Mass concentrated on the left; long tail extending to the right driven by positive outliers.

Positions of Central Tendencies:

  • Mode: \(x\)-value at the peak (maximum frequency) — far left.
  • Mean: Heavily influenced by extreme tail values — pulled far right.
  • Median: Splits area in half (50th percentile) — lies between Mode and Mean.

Empirical Rule for Right Skew: \(\text{Mean} > \text{Median} > \text{Mode}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify the distribution as right-skewed from the graph (long tail to the right).
  2. Mode = peak (leftmost); Mean = pulled rightward by tail; Median = between Mode and Mean.
  3. Moving left to right: Mode → Median → Mean, giving \(\text{Mean} > \text{Median} > \text{Mode}\).
  4. Evaluate options:
    • (A) Mean = Mode → False (symmetric distribution)
    • (B) Mean > Median but < Mode → False
    • (C) Mean > Median and Mean > Mode → True ✓
    • (D) Mode > Median → False (indicates left skew)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Mean is greater than median and mode | Correct option: (C)

questions.question:
All the members of the planar truss (see figure), have the same properties in terms of area of cross-section (A) and modulus of elasticity (E).



For the loads shown on the truss, the statement that correctly represents the nature of forces in the members of the truss is:
options: There are 3 members in tension, and 2 members in compression
There are 2 members in tension, 2 members in compression, and 1 zero-force member
There are 2 members in tension, 1 member in compression, and 2 zero-force members
There are 2 members in tension, and 3 zero-force members

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: There are 3 members in tension, and 2 members in compression
structuredOptions.html: There are 3 members in tension, and 2 members in compression

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: There are 2 members in tension, 2 members in compression, and 1 zero-force member
structuredOptions.html: There are 2 members in tension, 2 members in compression, and 1 zero-force member

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: There are 2 members in tension, 1 member in compression, and 2 zero-force members
structuredOptions.html: There are 2 members in tension, 1 member in compression, and 2 zero-force members

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: There are 2 members in tension, and 3 zero-force members
structuredOptions.html: There are 2 members in tension, and 3 zero-force members

questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Truss Analysis (Method of Joints / Sections)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Square truss with side length \(L\)
    • All members: same area \(A\) and modulus of elasticity \(E\)
    • Loading: Horizontal force \(P\) (leftward) at top-left joint D; Horizontal force \(P\) (rightward) at bottom-right joint B
    • Supports: Bottom-left (A) = roller (vertical restraint); Top-right (C) = pin (horizontal & vertical restraint)
  • Aim: Determine the nature of forces in all truss members (tension / compression / zero).

3. Core Concepts:

Method of Joints: \(\sum F_x = 0\) and \(\sum F_y = 0\) at each joint.

Zero-Force Member Rules:

  • If two non-collinear members meet at an unloaded joint → both are zero-force members.
  • If three members meet at an unloaded joint with two being collinear → the third is zero-force.

Sign Convention: Tension (+): member pulls the joint (force away from joint). Compression (−): member pushes the joint (force toward joint).

4. Solution Method:

Perform global equilibrium to find support reactions, then use joint equilibrium to determine member forces. Nodes are labelled: A (Bottom-Left), B (Bottom-Right), C (Top-Right), D (Top-Left).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Identify Unknown Reactions
    At A (roller): vertical reaction \(R_{Ay}\) only (horizontal free).
    At C (pin): \(R_{Cx}\) and \(R_{Cy}\).
    Note: A is a roller so \(R_{Ax} = 0\).
  2. Step 2: Global Equilibrium
    \(\sum F_x = 0\):\[R_{Cx} + P - P = 0 \implies R_{Cx} = 0 \]\(\sum M_A = 0\) (counter-clockwise positive):\[-(P \cdot L) + R_{Cx} \cdot L + R_{Cy} \cdot L = 0 \]\[-PL + 0 + R_{Cy} L = 0 \implies R_{Cy} = P \text{ (upward)} \]\(\sum F_y = 0\):\[R_{Ay} + R_{Cy} = 0 \implies R_{Ay} = -P \text{ (downward)} \]
  3. Step 3: Joint Analysis
    Joint D (Top-Left) — Load \(P\) leftward, members DA and DC:
    \(\sum F_x = 0\): \(F_{DC} = P\) (Tension)
    \(\sum F_y = 0\): \(F_{DA} = 0\) (Zero-force)

    Joint A (Bottom-Left) — Reaction \(R_{Ay} = P\) downward, members AD, AB, AC:
    \(F_{DA} = 0\) already known.
    \(\sum F_y = 0\): \(F_{AC}\sin 45^\circ = P \implies F_{AC} = P\sqrt{2}\) (Tension)
    \(\sum F_x = 0\): \(F_{AB} = F_{AC}\cos 45^\circ = P\) (Tension)

    Joint B (Bottom-Right) — Load \(P\) rightward, members BA and BC:
    \(\sum F_x = 0\): \(F_{AB} = P\) ✓ consistent.
    \(\sum F_y = 0\): \(F_{BC} = 0\) (Zero-force)

    Joint C (Top-Right) — Reactions \(R_{Cx} = 0\), \(R_{Cy} = P\) upward, members CD, CB, CA:
    \(F_{BC} = 0\), \(F_{DC} = P\): ✓ all balance.
  4. Step 4: Summary of Member Forces
    MemberForceNature
    AB (bottom chord)\(P\)Tension
    CD (top chord)\(P\)Tension
    AC (diagonal)\(P\sqrt{2}\)Tension
    AD (left vertical)0Zero-force
    BC (right vertical)0Zero-force

Conclusion: 2 tension members (AB, CD), 1 tension diagonal (AC), 2 zero-force members (AD, BC).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2 tension members and 3 zero-force members | Correct option: (D)

A vertical load of 10 kN acts on a hinge located at a distance of L/4 from the roller support Q of a beam of length L (see figure).



The vertical reaction at support Q is
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Statically Determinate Beams — Equilibrium

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application — static equilibrium of beams with internal hinges.
  • Given Data:
    ParameterValue
    Span\(L\)
    Load \(W\)10 kN (vertical)
    Support PFixed end
    Support QRoller
    Hinge location from P\(3L/4\)
    Hinge location from Q\(L/4\)
  • Aim: Find the vertical reaction at support Q (\(R_Q\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Key Principle: At an internal hinge, the bending moment is zero (\(M_{hinge} = 0\)). This provides an additional equilibrium equation beyond global equilibrium.

4. Solution Method:

Use the hinge condition — consider moment equilibrium from the right segment (hinge to Q) about the hinge point.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply Hinge Condition (right segment — hinge to Q):
    Forces on right segment: \(R_Q\) at Q (distance \(L/4\) from hinge); the 10 kN load acts at the hinge (zero moment arm).\[\sum M_{hinge}^{right} = 0 \implies R_Q \times \dfrac{L}{4} = 0 \implies R_Q = 0\text{ kN}\]
  2. Verification using Global Equilibrium:
    EquationExpressionResult
    \(\sum F_y = 0\)\(R_P + R_Q = 10\)\(R_P = 10\text{ kN}\)

ParameterValue
\(i_{cr}\)1.0
\(i_{exit}\)0.25
FS4.0

Final Answer: Factor of safety against piping = 4.0 | Correct option: (D)

The contact pressure and settlement distribution for a footing are shown in the figure.



The figure corresponds to a
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A figure showing contact pressure and settlement distribution profiles for a footing.
  • Aim: Identify the correct combination of footing rigidity and soil type corresponding to the figure.

3. Core Concepts:

Contact Pressure Distribution: Depends on the rigidity of the footing and the type of soil.

Soil Behaviour Summary:

Footing TypeSoil TypeContact PressureSettlement Profile
FlexibleClayUniformMax at centre (dish-shaped)
RigidClayMax at edges (saddle-shaped)Uniform
FlexibleGranular (Sand)UniformMax at edges
RigidGranular (Sand)Max at centre, zero at edgesUniform

4. Solution Method:

  1. Analyze the settlement constraint for a rigid footing (uniform settlement).
  2. Analyze the settlement behaviour of granular soil (edges settle more than centre under flexible load).
  3. Apply the logic of "compensation": to reduce the high natural settlement at the edges of sand, the contact pressure at the edges must be reduced.
  4. Conclude the contact pressure distribution profile.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Characterize the Footing: A rigid footing enforces uniform settlement: \(S = \text{constant}\) at all points.
  2. Characterize the Soil (Granular/Sand): Soil stiffness is low near the edges (low confining pressure) and high near the centre. Under a flexible footing with uniform pressure, edges would settle much more than the centre.
  3. Interaction Analysis for Rigid Footing on Granular Soil:
    • The footing forces \(S_{edge} = S_{centre}\).
    • Since edge soil is "soft" (prone to more settlement), the footing must apply less pressure at the edges to limit settlement there.
    • Since centre soil is "stiff", the footing carries a higher load at the centre.
    • Result: Contact pressure is maximum at the centre and drops to zero at the edges; settlement is uniform.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Rigid footing on granular soil | Correct option: (A)

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties & Exploration

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Conceptual / Recall
  • Given Data: Four statements regarding soil mechanics principles.
  • Aim: Identify the statement that is NOT correct.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Consistency Limits: Plastic state = water content between Plastic Limit (PL) and Liquid Limit (LL).
  • Boussinesq's Theory: Assumes homogeneous, isotropic, semi-infinite, elastic medium — used for point loads on the surface.
  • Westergaard's Theory: Assumes stratified (layered) deposits with thin rigid sheets — specifically for layered soils.
  • Slope Stability: Stability Number method (Taylor's chart).
  • SPT Corrections (IS 2131): Overburden and Dilatancy corrections for saturated fine sands.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Statement (A): "When the water content lies between liquid limit and plastic limit, the soil is in plastic state." — This is the textbook definition. Correct ✓
  2. Statement (B): "Boussinesq's theory is used for the analysis of stratified soil." — Boussinesq's solution applies to a homogeneous, isotropic elastic medium. It does not account for stratification. Westergaard's theory is specifically derived for stratified deposits. Incorrect ✗
  3. Statement (C): "The inclination of a stable slope in cohesive soil can be greater than its angle of internal friction." — For purely cohesive soil (\(\phi = 0\)), a vertical cut (90°) is theoretically stable up to critical height \(H_c = 4c/\gamma\). Since \(90° > 0°\), this is physically possible. Correct ✓
  4. Statement (D): "For saturated dense fine sand, after overburden correction, if SPT value exceeds 15, dilatancy correction is to be applied." — Per IS 2131 Clause 5.2, corrected \(N'' = 15 + 0.5(N' - 15)\) when \(N' > 15\). Correct ✓

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Statement B is incorrect | Correct option: (B)

questions.question: Probability (up to one decimal place) of consecutively picking 3 red balls without replacement from a box containing 5 red balls and 1 white ball is ______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability Theory — Sampling Without Replacement

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Red balls = 5, White balls = 1; Total = 6; 3 balls drawn consecutively without replacement.
  • Aim: Calculate the probability that all 3 drawn balls are red.

3. Core Concepts:

Conditional Probability (without replacement):\[P(\text{3 red}) = \dfrac{R}{T} \times \dfrac{R-1}{T-1} \times \dfrac{R-2}{T-2}\]where \(R\) = red balls, \(T\) = total balls.

Alternative (Combinatorial): \(\dfrac{\binom{5}{3}}{\binom{6}{3}}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial state: 5 red, 1 white → Total = 6
    \(P_1 = \dfrac{5}{6}\)
  2. After 1 red drawn: 4 red, 1 white → Total = 5
    \(P_2 = \dfrac{4}{5}\)
  3. After 2 red drawn: 3 red, 1 white → Total = 4
    \(P_3 = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
  4. Combined probability:\[P = \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{60}{120} = 0.5\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.5 | Accepted range: 0.5 to 0.5

questions.question: The quadratic equation \( 2x^2 - 3x + 3 = 0 \) is to be solved numerically starting with an initial guess as \( x_0 = 2 \). The new estimate of \( x \) after the first iteration using Newton-Raphson method is ______
questions.explanation:
Numerical Methods | Newton-Raphson Method for Root Finding

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Equation \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 3 = 0\); initial guess \(x_0 = 2\); first iteration of Newton-Raphson.
  • Aim: Find the new estimate \(x_1\).

3. Core Concepts:

Newton-Raphson Formula:\[x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}\]

Function and derivative:\[f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 3 \qquad f'(x) = 4x - 3\]

Note: Discriminant \(= (-3)^2 - 4(2)(3) = -15 < 0\) (no real roots), but the iteration is still computable.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate at \(x_0 = 2\):\[f(2) = 2(4) - 3(2) + 3 = 8 - 6 + 3 = 5\]\[f'(2) = 4(2) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5\]
  2. Apply Newton-Raphson formula:\[x_1 = 2 - \dfrac{5}{5} = 2 - 1 = 1\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1 | Accepted range: 1 to 1

questions.question: A reinforced-concrete slab with effective depth of 80 mm is simply supported at two opposite ends on 230 mm thick masonry walls. The centre-to-centre distance between the walls is 3.3 m. As per IS 456 : 2000, the effective span of the slab (in m, up to two decimal places) is ______

Reinforced Concrete Design | Effective Span of Slabs per IS 456:2000

  • Given Data:

    • Support width (masonry wall): \(230\text{ mm} = 0.23\text{ m}\)
    • Centre-to-centre distance between walls: \(3.3\text{ m}\)
    • Code: IS 456:2000
  • Aim: Calculate effective span of simply supported slab (in m).

IS 456:2000 Clause 22.2(a): Effective span for simply supported slabs:\[l_{eff} = \min\left\{l_0 + d,\ \text{centre-to-centre of supports}\right\}\]where \(l_0\) = clear span, \(d\) = effective depth of slab.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate clear span (\(l_0\)):\[l_0 = 3.3 - 0.23 = 3.07\text{ m}\]
  2. First candidate (clear span + effective depth):\[l_1 = l_0 + d = 3.07 + 0.08 = 3.15\text{ m}\]
  3. Second candidate (c/c distance):\[l_2 = 3.3\text{ m}\]
  4. Apply IS 456:2000 Clause 22.2(a):\[l_{eff} = \min\{3.15,\ 3.3\} = 3.15\text{ m}\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.15 m | Accepted range: 3.15 to 3.15

questions.question: A fillet weld is simultaneously subjected to factored normal and shear stresses of 120 MPa and 50 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800 : 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Steel Design | Equivalent Stress in Fillet Welds per IS 800:2007

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Factored normal stress: \(f_a = 120\text{ MPa}\)
    • Factored shear stress: \(q = 50\text{ MPa}\)
    • Code: IS 800:2007
  • Aim: Calculate equivalent stress in fillet weld (in MPa).

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 Clause 10.5.10.1.1: Equivalent stress for combined loading in fillet welds:\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2}\]where \(f_a\) = normal stress perpendicular to weld throat; \(q\) = shear stress on weld throat.

Pitfall: Do not use \(f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + q^2}\) — the factor of 3 with the shear term is essential (von Mises criterion).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Write the formula:\[f_e = \sqrt{f_a^2 + 3q^2}\]
  2. Substitute values:\[f_e = \sqrt{(120)^2 + 3 \times (50)^2}\]
  3. Compute terms:\[(120)^2 = 14400, \quad (50)^2 = 2500, \quad 3 \times 2500 = 7500\]
  4. Sum and evaluate:\[f_e = \sqrt{14400 + 7500} = \sqrt{21900} = 147.99\text{ MPa}\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 147.99 MPa | Accepted range: 147.50 to 148.50
